name: Freelancer
title: Free Freelancer Invoice Template
description: A free freelancer invoice template for hourly or fixed-fee work: project name, hours, rate, payment terms and how to pay you. Fill it in online, download a PDF.
summary: Hours × rate, with the project named at the top and the terms in the side column.
intro: Your hours and rate, the project the work belongs to, and the terms you agreed, set out so a client can approve it without writing back. Free to fill in and download as a PDF.
explanation: When you freelance, the invoice is often the only document a client’s finance team sees. They didn’t brief you and they don’t know the project, so the invoice has to explain itself: who you are, what the work was, which project or purchase order it belongs to, and when and how to pay.

This template puts the project directly under the title and uses Hours and Rate columns, so time-based work reads naturally. Fixed fees work too: a quantity of 1 and the fee as the rate. Your details, the client, the dates and the payment terms sit in a side column, away from the figures.

It suits writers, designers, developers, editors, translators, virtual assistants, researchers and anyone billing their own time. If you don’t yet have a routine, read [how to invoice as a freelancer](/invoice-guides/how-to-invoice-as-a-freelancer/).
fieldsTitle: What to put on a freelance invoice

fields.name: Your name or business
fields.text: The name you trade under, with an email and, if you have them, a website and tax ID. A sole trader’s own name is fine.

fields.name: Project or PO
fields.text: The project name, and the client’s purchase order number if they gave you one. Many companies can’t pay an invoice without it.

fields.name: Work and hours
fields.text: Each piece of work with the hours spent and your rate. Group small tasks; split the work the client will recognize.

fields.name: Fixed fees
fields.text: For a fixed-price job, a quantity of 1 and the agreed fee. You can mix fixed and hourly lines.

fields.name: Expenses
fields.text: Agreed expenses at cost, such as software, travel or stock images, as their own lines.

fields.name: Payment terms
fields.text: When payment is due (Net 14 or Net 30 are common) and any late fee you agreed in your contract.

fields.name: How to pay you
fields.text: Bank details, a payment link or both. The easier it is, the sooner it happens.

steps.title: Open the example
steps.text: Customize this invoice opens a freelance invoice in the generator. Your saved name and details are kept.

steps.title: Name the project
steps.text: Enter the client and the project (and PO number if there is one), then each piece of work with hours and rate.

steps.title: Terms and payment
steps.text: Pick your payment terms; the due date is set for you. Add your bank details or payment link.

steps.title: Download and send
steps.text: Download the PDF and email it to whoever pays invoices, not only your contact. See [how to send an invoice](/invoice-guides/how-to-send-an-invoice/).

faqs.q: What should a freelance invoice include?
faqs.a: Your name and contact details, the client’s name and address, an invoice number, the issue and due dates, a description of the work with hours or fees, the total, and how to pay. Add a tax ID and tax where they apply. The full list is in [what to put on an invoice](/invoice-guides/what-to-put-on-an-invoice/).

faqs.q: Can I invoice without a registered business?
faqs.a: In many countries, including the US and the UK, you can invoice as an individual under your own name. You may still need to register for tax once you earn above a threshold; check the rules where you live.

faqs.q: Should I bill hourly or by the project?
faqs.a: Both are common. Hourly suits open-ended work; a fixed fee suits work with a clear scope. This template handles either, and you can combine them on one invoice.

faqs.q: How do I add a late fee?
faqs.a: Only charge one you agreed in advance, usually in your contract. State it in the notes (“Late payments incur a 1.5% monthly fee”), and if a payment is late, add the fee as a line on a follow-up invoice.
